gpt.text:
Run the three commands in order; they implement the standard “pick best module → run full system candidates → generate next-fix plan” loop. Given your current state (no PASS candidates, no inconclusive), this is a clean cycle.

## 1) Select best module candidate (AUB autopilot)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
```
What it does:
- Executes module-level experiments defined in `module_registry.yaml`.
- Promotes the best-performing candidate (if it meets your pass criteria) into the “current champion” slot or updates the champion reference used downstream.

What to verify after it runs:
- It should print which candidate (if any) was selected and why.
- Check the resulting champion file/update (often it writes/updates something adjacent to `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` or updates that file, depending on your tooling).
- Confirm whether you now have a PASS candidate; your handoff shows none, so this is the step that could produce one.

## 2) Run system-level candidates
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
```
What it does:
- Runs end-to-end/system evaluations for candidates specified in `system_candidates.yaml` (typically using whatever the module step selected or whatever the spec defines).
- Produces system metrics and determines PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE per system candidate.

What to verify after it runs:
- A report artifact location (often a `baseline/reports/...` or similar folder).
- Whether any system candidates are marked PASS (and any regressions vs the champion).

## 3) Generate the “next fix” action plan
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What it does:
- Summarizes failures/regressions and proposes the next module-level fixes/experiments to try.
- Writes the plan to `baseline/reports/next_fix.md`.

What to verify after it runs:
- That `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` was generated and contains concrete suggested changes/tests (not empty).
- Any referenced module IDs exist in `module_registry.yaml`.

## Notes on your current metrics
- You have champion stats:
  - `tuning_mean/min: 1.9038 / 0.4315`
  - `lockbox_mean/min: 1.7925 / 1.1337`
- Whether “lower is better” depends on your scoring definition. If these are loss-like metrics, lower is better; if they’re reward-like, higher is better. The autopilot scripts typically encode the directionality—just ensure it matches your intended objective.

If you paste the console output (or the generated report paths) from step 1 and step 2, I can help interpret whether the selection logic behaved correctly and whether any candidate should be promoted.
